Rules for route planning
New staff will learn how the first steps go

This page explains why careful route planning matters at Aurelia Skyways and how it supports safe, orderly service through the Companion Animal Travel Desk. Every booking must be checked with attention to the animal, the route, and the needs of the traveler, because small errors can delay care or prevent acceptance at the airport. New staff should read each file as a whole and confirm that the travel plan matches the reservation record, the animal profile, and the current acceptance rules before any promise is given to the customer.

When reviewing a small dog case, begin with the core eligibility notes and then confirm the supporting documents. <<FACT F074>> The health record must also be examined for completeness and clarity, and any gap should be raised through the proper review path rather than guessed at by the agent. <<FACT F080>> If the traveler has selected a routing option that creates a connection, the desk must verify whether the animal can remain comfortable and whether the receiving station is prepared to continue the handoff without confusion.

The cabin team monitors animals during flight, and staff must communicate any concern in calm, direct language. Every animal receives patient attention from trained staff, and the first response to a problem is to check the facts, then escalate through the standard stepwise review. Do not give casual assurances, do not skip a document review, and do not assume that a previous trip creates a current approval. Use the same careful method for each case, whether the traveler is experienced or new to the process.

Remember to keep the record complete, the tone steady, and the route decision aligned with policy.
